episodes.162074: Convergence ahead of an approaching front combined with ample Gulf moisture led to the development of thunderstorms early on the morning of September 30th. Gusty winds accompanied some of these storms, a few of which became severe. During this event, a severe storm impacted the Brownsville airport, which reported a wind gust to 52 knots/60 mph.
episodes.162310: A strengthening upper level low pressure system was over Arizona and New Mexico with attached upper disturbances that moved over West Texas. High low-level moisture values were across the area. A cold front was pushing through the region, and there was a dryline across the Lower Trans Pecos and Permian Basin. Daytime heating allowed for the atmosphere to become unstable. These conditions resulted in thunderstorms that produced strong, damaging winds and hail across West Texas.
episodes.163120: A cluster of thunderstorms near the Matagorda Bay and offshore in the late morning hours continued to develop to the southwest along the Middle Texas coast in the afternoon. Some of the storms produced wind gusts to 35 knots.
episodes.163123: Locally heavy rainfall from thunderstorms produced flooding of roads in the Annaville.
episodes.163163: A dryline and weak upper wave helped initiate storms across far southwest Oklahoma and also in portions of northwest Oklahoma during the late afternoon. Storms persisted for several hours into the evening with a few reports of severe hail received.
episodes.163193: Heavy rainfall led to a localized flood.
episodes.163216: On September 29th, a cold front moved through northwestern Kansas which caused a line of thunderstorms to move across the area. These thunderstorms produced hail up to nickel in size along with localized heavy rainfall.
episodes.163365: The combination of moderate instability and a weak upper level disturbance resulted in scattered thunderstorms across much of west central Texas. A few storms were severe.
episodes.163762: A shortwave trough rotating around an upper level low near the four corner region pushed in some rain showers and stronger thunderstorms, isolated in nature, along the Oklahoma state line. There was ample enough instability to produce a half dollar sized hail report.

events.narrative: Report received of pea to nickel sized hail at location.
The Brownsville/South Padre Island International Airport recorded a wind gust to 52 knots/60 mph as severe thunderstorms moved through the area.
Water over road and driveway cutting off house.
A thunderstorm moved across Andrews County and produced a 62 mph wind gust near the town of Andrews.
Mesonet station at Bayside measured a gust to 37 knots.
An Amateur Radio operator reported a semi truck blown over, a pivot irrigation system blown down and two power poles toppled.
A thunderstorm moved across Scurry County and produced wind damage. There were downed power lines and tree limbs. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
A thunderstorm produced quarter sized hail ten miles southwest of McDonald Observatory. There was lots of quarter sized hail covering the ground at Bloys Camp.
A thunderstorm produced a 61 mph wind gust near Snyder.
TCOON site at Nueces Bay measured a gust to 36 knots.
Several areas in Annaville were flooded with vehicles stalled in high water. Water was over the intersection of Rand Morgan and Leopard Street.
Law enforcement reports high water rescues ongoing in Abilene. Also, a flooded home was reported at the 1200 block of Westmoreland St.
A thunderstorm moved across Terrell County and produced a 71 mph wind gust in Dryden.
